detail:
MedlinePlus describes hay fever, the seasonal form of allergic rhinitis, as an allergic reaction triggered when pollen from trees, weeds, and grasses is inhaled and reaches the nose and throat. Allergic rhinitis more broadly is a group of symptoms affecting the nose that occur after breathing in something a person is allergic to, such as pollen, dust, or animal dander. The immune system response described in the sources involves antibodies and the release of histamine, which produces itching, swelling, and mucus.

Symptoms can include sneezing, often with a runny or clogged nose, coughing and postnasal drip, itching of the eyes, nose, and throat, and red, watery eyes. MedlinePlus notes that a health care provider may diagnose hay fever based on a physical exam and symptoms, and that skin or blood tests are sometimes used to identify the specific allergens involved. Sources distinguish seasonal allergic rhinitis, tied to pollen seasons, from year-round symptoms tied to indoor allergens such as dust mites, mold, and animal dander.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about allergic rhinitis symptoms and allergy testing.
summary: MedlinePlus describes allergic rhinitis, called hay fever when pollen is the trigger, as an allergic reaction affecting the nose and eyes, with symptoms that can include sneezing, congestion, and itchy, watery eyes, diagnosed from exam, symptoms, and sometimes allergy tests.
takeaways: pollen, dust, and dander are common triggers described
symptoms can include sneezing, congestion, and itchy eyes
diagnosis may use exam, symptoms, and skin or blood tests
title: Allergic rhinitis: hay fever and the reaction to inhaled allergens
